content: Thymol is a monoterpene phenol derived from cymene, with the chemical formula C10H13OH. It is isomeric with carvacrol and is naturally found in the essential oil of thyme. Thymol is extracted as a white crystalline substance that possesses a pleasant aromatic odor and exhibits strong antiseptic properties. It is also referred to as hydroxy cymene. One minor application of thymol is in the field of bookbinding. Specifically, books that have been damaged by mold can be sealed in bags containing thymol crystals prior to rebinding. This process effectively eliminates fungal spores. Thymol is also utilized as a preservative in halothane, an anesthetic agent. In a 1994 report published by five major cigarette companies, thymol was identified as one of the 599 additives used in the production of cigarettes. In this context, thymol is added to enhance the flavor of the product.
